questionText:
In an Entity-Relationship (ER) model, suppose $R$ is a many-to-one relationship from entity set E1 to entity set E2. Assume that E1 and E2 participate totally in $R$ and that the cardinality of E1 is greater than the cardinality of E2.

Which one of the following is true about $R$?
options: Every entity in E1 is associated with exactly one entity in E2.
Some entity in E1 is associated with more than one entity in E2.
Every entity in E2 is associated with exactly one entity in E1.
Every entity in E2 is associated with at most one entity in E1.
explanation:
Step 1: Understand Many-to-One Mapping Constraint
In a many-to-one relationship $R$ from entity set $E1$ to entity set $E2$, any single entity in $E1$ can be associated with at most one entity in $E2$.

Step 2: Apply Total Participation
Total participation of $E1$ in $R$ means that every entity in $E1$ must participate in $R$. Therefore, each entity in $E1$ must be associated with at least one entity in $E2$.

Step 3: Combine Constraints
Combining 'at least one' (from total participation) and 'at most one' (from the many-to-one constraint), every entity in $E1$ must be associated with exactly one entity in $E2$.

Hence, option (A) is correct.
